input.task: Who wrote the quote about thinking?

provenance: M38, rung 2. Deployment run e985e048 (quotes.toscrape.com): `extract {text: "Albert Einstein"}` resolved to 3 matches and the run died `ResolveError: 3 matches at tier text` — three elements that say the same thing, on a page whose answer was the string being matched. Rung 1 cannot help: the identity anchor of such a task IS the author name, so it matches the candidates themselves and identifies no single place (NEAREST_JS returns AMBIGUOUS, which the anchor rung swallows rather than raising — only an explicit `near` is loud about it). Watched red first: `status failure:locate`, reason `ambiguous-match: 3 matches at tier text for {'text': 'Marisol Vance'}` (no relocation rung: the text tier is already used and <small> carries no accessible name for the role+name rung).

triage.what_this_grades: the narrow case where picking the first match in document order cannot change the answer: every match has the same role AND the same reading, the plan carried no `index`, the action reads rather than acts, and the task asks for one thing. Take any conjunct away and this rung is a silent-wrong-answer generator, which is why each has a case: resolver-narrows-by-anchor-proximity (same role, different readings), resolver-refuses-mixed-roles (same reading, different roles), resolver-refuses-plural-wording (a task asking for more than one), l4-shop-duplicate-labels (a CLICK on two same-named buttons, which must still fail and relocate).
triage.not_covered: matches that read the same today and diverge tomorrow — the check is over the rendered text at resolve time, not a promise about the page.
